judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claims all hold; I checked each conversion independently. P(-3, 4) is in QII so th = 180 - 53.13 = 126.87; Q(2, -2) is in QIV so th = 315, not 135; (-4, 60 deg) has y = -4 sin 60 = -3.46 with the point in QIII; x = 3 sin(pi/3) = 2.60; y = 2 sin t = 1 on the ellipse gives t = 30 and 150 degrees; R(-5, -12) is in QIII so th = 180 + 67.38 = 247.38; and (-6, 200 deg) renames to (6, 20 deg). The problem-8 synthesis is right too: cos(-t) = cos t and sin(-t) = -sin t, both curves satisfy (x-2)^2 + (y+1)^2 = 9, and the key's t-table puts C1 at (2, 2) and C2 at (2, -4) after a quarter turn. What the 32/32 misses is an instruction-following gap written into the sheet's own directions: "Where a student's work is shown, (i) name the error in one sentence, then (ii) give the corrected value." Each of problems 1-7 therefore prints a diagnosis slot as well as a value, and all seven are recorded as machine-checkable types (approx, solve_interval, eval) with only problem 8 typed manual. The answer key proves the second slot exists -- its preamble reads "Give credit for the diagnosis separately from the number: a student who fixes the value but cannot say why the first answer failed will repeat the error" -- yet the verification data declares nothing for it, on a prompt that says to label any genuinely open response for manual review. Two narrower findings: problem 6 also asks "Which quadrant does R actually lie in?", a discrete checkable answer (III) with no entry, and problem 2 asks the student to SKETCH the point, a drawn representation inside a machine-verified item. Finally, the prompt says "Declare any planted wrong results as machine-checked misconception traps", and problem 5 plants one (the student answers "t = 30 deg" and stops) that is NOT declared -- because scripts/verify.py's _TRAP_TYPES excludes solve_interval, so a trap cannot be attached to a list-valued answer at all. Six of the seven planted results are declared; the seventh is unmeetable under the current contract.

strengths_to_preserve: Six declared traps whose wrong-METHOD expressions reproduce exactly the numbers printed in the students' shown work -- atan(4/(-3)) -> -53.13, 180 + atan(-2/2) -> 135, 4 sin 60 -> 3.46, 3 cos(pi/3) -> 1.5, atan(12/5) -> 67.38, 200 + 180 -> 380. The worksheet's fiction and the key's "Common wrong answers" block come from the same declarations.

The answer key's diagnosis-then-repair shape, with the diagnosis named precisely: problem 6 explains that the two minus signs cancelled inside -12/-5 so the calculator returned the QI reference angle, and problem 2 distinguishes that adding 180 reverses a direction while adding 360 renames it. These are the sentences a student cannot write unaided.

Problem 8's manual entry is paired with a model answer containing the four-row t-table, the shared Cartesian equation, and an explicit three-part acceptance standard (same circle equation; two matched t values proving opposite directions; the statement that orientation is information the Cartesian equation does not carry).

Problem 7 is the sharpest item on the sheet: 380 deg and 20 deg name the same ray, so the key can say the direction was right and only the naming was wrong -- "an answer outside the stated interval is not yet an answer" -- which separates a conceptual error from a bookkeeping one.

root_causes.description: The contract has no way to say that a problem carries both a machine-checkable value and a human-graded diagnosis, so an error-analysis sheet whose whole point is naming the error records only the repaired numbers and reports itself as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet directions: "(i) name the error in one sentence, then (ii) give the corrected value" -- problems 1-7 all print both
verify.json types problems 1-7 as approx/solve_interval/eval with no manual companion; only problem 8 is manual
the answer key's preamble instructs "Give credit for the diagnosis separately from the number" -- the key grades a slot the data does not declare
worksheet problem 2 also asks the student to sketch the point, and problem 6 asks which quadrant R lies in, with no entry for either

root_causes.description: Misconception traps are restricted to types with a single comparable scalar answer, so a planted wrong result that is an INCOMPLETE SOLUTION SET -- the commonest error-analysis fiction on a trigonometric or parametric item -- cannot be declared or machine-checked at all.
evidence: scripts/verify.py _TRAP_TYPES omits solve, solve_interval and system; validate_traps raises "type ... cannot carry traps -- a trap needs a single comparable answer to be distinguishable from"
worksheet problem 5 plants "t = 30 deg" and stops, against the verified set [30, 150]; verify.json id 5 declares no trap
task prompt: "Declare any planted wrong results as machine-checked misconception traps"

improvements.title: Seven find-and-fix items require a named diagnosis and none is declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a build gate tests/check_open_response_flags.py, wired into scripts/build.sh next to check_layout.py, that reads the ws_ .tex and the verify JSON together. For each problem body it matches explanation cues (explain / justify / name the error / name the first wrong line / say in one sentence / say what / describe / sketch / state what it tells you / why) and fails the build when that problem id carries no entry of type `manual`. Tighten SKILL.md's rule from "Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer" to the explicit statement that a problem mixing a computed answer with a written justification needs BOTH entries under the same id -- the multi-entry-per-id shape verify.py already supports and that curr-445 already uses correctly.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_open_response_flags.py::test_explanation_without_manual_entry_fails -- a fixture worksheet whose problem 2 reads "Solve ... then explain in one sentence why the negative candidate is extraneous" with verify.json holding only {"id": 2, "type": "solve", ...} must exit non-zero and name problem 2; the same fixture with an added {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry must exit 0. Today no such gate exists, so the first fixture builds green.
improvements.expected_impact: Every written justification the sheet demands becomes visible as a manual-review item (exit 2) instead of being absorbed into a "fully machine-verified" claim, which is what the task prompt asks for.
improvements.risk: Cue matching over prose will over-fire on stems that merely say "show your work"; keep the cue list narrow, exempt ids already typed `manual`, and fixture-lock both the firing and the non-firing case.

improvements.title: Problem 6's quadrant answer and problem 2's sketch are printed demands with no check
improvements.proposed_change: Make the answer-slot count explicit and checked. Add a per-id integer `slots` to the verify JSON contract -- the number of distinct responses the printed problem asks the student to write -- and make scripts/verify.py hard-fail (exit 1) when the number of entries under an id is smaller than its declared `slots`. Change the SKILL.md rule from "every problem id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed answer demand has its own check", and have tests/check_layout.py cross-check `slots` against the enumerated parts and answer-location macros it already counts, so an under-declared `slots` is caught as well.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_error_paths.py::test_slot_count_greater_than_entry_count_fails -- a verify fixture with {"id": 4, "type": "eval", ..., "slots": 5} and a single entry for id 4 must exit 1 naming the four uncovered slots; the same fixture with five entries under id 4 must exit 0. Today `slots` is an unknown field that the strict schema rejects outright, so neither branch can be expressed.
improvements.expected_impact: A problem that prints four named parameters and an evaluation can no longer ship with one check covering the evaluation alone, and the generated Quick Answers bank gains the missing entries for free, since it renders from the same data.
improvements.risk: `slots` is author-declared and can be under-counted; the layout cross-check is what keeps it honest, and it must tolerate genuinely single-slot problems with multi-sentence stems.

improvements.title: A planted incomplete solution set cannot be declared as a trap
improvements.proposed_change: Extend traps to list-valued answers. Add solve and solve_interval to _TRAP_TYPES in scripts/verify.py and let a trap on those types declare a wrong SET: `expr` evaluates to a list (or a single root) and check_traps passes when the trap's set differs from the verified set -- a dropped root, an extra extraneous root, or a shifted family. The existing rule that the trap's value is DERIVED from a wrong method, never typed, carries over unchanged. Update the SKILL.md trap table so error-analysis sheets can declare the incomplete-answer fiction they most often plant.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_facets.py::test_trap_on_solution_set -- a verify fixture with {"id": 5, "type": "solve_interval", "expr": "2*sin(t) - 1", "interval": [0, 360], "unit": "deg", "expected": [30, 150], "traps": [{"desc": "read only the arcsin value and stopped", "expr": "[30]"}]} must exit 0 or 2 and print the trap in the common-wrong-answers block. Today it exits 1 with "type 'solve_interval' cannot carry traps".
improvements.expected_impact: Error-analysis worksheets can machine-check every planted wrong result, including the dominant one on trigonometric and parametric items, instead of leaving the incompleteness fiction undeclared.
improvements.risk: Set comparison must not pass a trap that equals the verified set, which would print the right answer as a wrong one; assert strict inequality and fixture-lock the failing case as well as the passing one.

case_summary: A first-rate misconception packet: seven quadrant and orientation errors, each shown as real student work, each diagnosed before it is repaired, with six machine-derived traps and a genuinely open synthesis on parametric orientation. All the mathematics is correct. The gap the judge did not record is that the sheet's own directions demand a named diagnosis on every shown-work item and the answer key instructs the grader to score it separately, yet all seven are typed as machine checks with no manual companion -- the one slot carrying this sheet's learning objective is the slot nothing declares. A second, contract-level finding: problem 5's planted wrong result is an incomplete solution set and could not have been declared as a trap even had the author tried, because traps are restricted to single-scalar types.
